page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, but lacks AMX support.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core score of 1575.58 and multi-core score of 12474.34 align with mid-range capabilities. Memory bandwidth tests show 698.22 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 55.6 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. While database operations and Redis SET performance (11.64 million operations per second) remain average, the instance exhibits weaknesses in specific areas. Passmark memory tests and CPU physics simulations fall into the bottom 25% performance tier. Additionally, LLM inference tasks on a 7B model are limited, yielding a weak text generation speed of 6.99 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute resources without the risk of shared-core degradation, though the lack of bundled local storage requires external storage provisioning. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance applicable for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving (measured at 7.8 GB/sec), standard database operations, and lightweight single-threaded or multi-threaded decompression tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.3xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 12 dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB vCPUs running at 3.2 GHz and 48.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks generally fall within the average tier, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12474.34 and Redis SET performance of 11.64 million operations per second. However, the instance shows performance limitations in Passmark memory tests and CPU physics simulations, which rank in the bottom 25%. With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance supports standard database operations, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing workloads that do not require high-speed local storage or heavy memory bandwidth.
